extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians, philosophers, and students interested in foundations of mathematics and intuitionism
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts and presents foundational standards and methodological criteria from Brouwer's lectures on intuitionism: what counts as mathematical existence, acceptable logical principles, constructive methods for continuum and sequences, and how mathematical truth is to be judged. Aimed at understanding or applying intuitionistic principles in foundations or constructive mathematics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Origin of mathematical entities: basic intuition of twoity/time
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematics is an essentially languageless activity of the mind having its origin in the perception of a move of time (the 'twoity' — a life moment falling apart into two, retained by memory).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inner experience (twoity → unity → twoity+unity → threeity → sequence) is the constructive source: by unlimited unfolding of this basic intuition many mathematical entities (including natural numbers and further systems) are built. Mathematics must be traced back to such constructive mental acts rather than to linguistic axioms or external objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of mathematics from mathematical language
rubrics_metrics.description: Completely separate mathematics from mathematical language: mathematical constructions are languageless; language only serves as an efficient but not infallible technique for memorising and communicating constructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because language is merely a mnemonic/communicative tool, linguistic formulations cannot be taken as creating mathematical objects or guaranteeing their existence; one must check whether a linguistic application of logical principles corresponds to an actual languageless mathematical procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of classical logical principles: accept contradiction and syllogism; reject excluded middle in general
rubrics_metrics.description: The principles of contradiction and syllogism may be affirmed (allowing for the inadequacy of language), but the principle of the excluded third (tertius exclusus) cannot in general serve as an instrument for discovering new mathematical truths and is rejected except in special cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications of the law of excluded middle are legitimate in contexts where the assertion can be decided by a finite constructive procedure (bounded finite constructions). For general/infinite mathematical assertions, using excluded middle is not justified because it would imply every assertion is decidable independent of human thought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legitimacy of excluded middle in finite/bounded cases
rubrics_metrics.description: For every construction of a bounded finite nature in a finite mathematical system, the application of the principle of the excluded third is legitimate because each attempt can be decided in a finite number of steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assertions about the possibility of finite bounded constructions are decidable by exhaustive finite trials; hence in such cases either proof or refutation can be attained and excluded-middle reasoning is acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical truth as activity-dependent: threefold status of assertions
rubrics_metrics.description: A mathematical assertion can be: (1) proved true, (2) proved absurd, or (3) neither proved true nor absurd and lacking a known finite algorithm to decide it. Truth is confined to mathematical activity and not an extrinsic property independent of human thought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides an introspective, constructivist theory of assertions: cases (1) and (2) are permanent; case (3) may later change if a constructive method is found. One must judge assertions by available constructive methods, not by appeal to an omniscient external truth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fleeing property (definition and criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'fleeing property' f is one that (i) for each natural number n it can be decided whether n has f, (ii) no way of calculating an n possessing f is known, and (iii) the assumption that at least one n possesses f is not known to be absurd.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such properties illustrate undecidable-but-meaningful assertions in intuitionism (example: whether a certain digit block occurs somewhere in pi's decimal expansion). A fleeing property may later cease to be fleeing if a witness is found or absurdity proved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject composing the continuum from predeterminate point-sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Classical attempts to compose the continuum from real numbers determined by predeterminate convergent infinite sequences yield only an ever-unfinished denumerable species of measure zero and so fail to produce a genuine continuum of positive measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hilbert-style completeness axioms or other purely linguistic/logical constructions that postulate an ultimate extension are regarded as producing only linguistic continua; intuitionism demands genuine mathematical continua constructed by constructive means.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admit freely proceeding infinite sequences to construct continuum
rubrics_metrics.description: Intuitionism admits two ways of creating new entities: (1) freely proceeding infinite sequences of previously acquired entities (so decimal fractions need not have exact values or guarantees of ever getting exact values), and (2) mathematical species (properties) defined for previously acquired entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By allowing freely proceeding sequences, intuitionistic mathematics replaces the linguistic continuum with a genuine mathematical continuum of positive measure. This constructive admission is essential for analysis and for going beyond 'separable' mathematics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical species and equality (closure and equivalence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematical species are properties supposable for previously acquired entities, with the condition that if they hold for a certain entity they also hold for all entities defined to be 'equal' to it; equality definitions must satisfy symmetry, reflexivity and transitivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Species are constructive collections determined by properties closed under the chosen notion of equality; defining equality properly (an equivalence relation) is required for species to behave coherently in further constructive development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Axioms and linguistic postulates are not foundational for construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Axioms introduced by logical or linguistic means (e.g., axiom of completeness) are considered linguistic and do not confer genuine mathematical existence; intuitionism rejects creating mathematics from such axioms external to constructive intuition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where classical methods postulate ultimate extensions or completeness, intuitionists demand constructive procedures (e.g., freely proceeding sequences) rather than acceptance of axioms without sensory or epistemological evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concrete decidability criterion for existence assertions
rubrics_metrics.description: Existence assertions concerning bounded finite constructions are decidable by finite exhaustive methods; for infinite constructions, decidability requires exhibiting a constructive procedure — otherwise such existence assertions may be neither provable nor absurd.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between finite constructive existence (decidable by search) and infinite/existential claims where one must present a construction or accept undecidability; do not rely on nonconstructive existence proofs via excluded middle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intuitionistic theorems arise from compulsory developmental constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Theorems holding in intuitionistic but not classical mathematics often originate from the fact that for entities in a species the imposition of a property enforces a special character on their development from the basic intuition; from this compulsory character follow properties false classically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include: the continuum does not split, and every full function on the unit continuum is necessarily uniformly continuous. Expect intuitionistic results to reflect restrictions coming from constructive growth processes rather than classical pointwise constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language inadequacy and correspondence check
rubrics_metrics.description: When mathematical language formulates what appears to be an application of classical logical principles, one must check whether the linguistic figure accompanies an actual languageless mathematical procedure; language is inevitably inadequate and may misrepresent mathematical operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat linguistic formulations as automatic evidence of constructive procedures. A careful examination is required to ensure that language corresponds to genuine constructive acts; failure to do so leads to unjustified classical inferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical stock as personal and communal constructive reality
rubrics_metrics.description: The stock of mathematical entities is a real thing for each person and for humanity; mathematics is an interior constructional activity that can be applied but does not depend on an exterior world in its origin or methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This epistemological stance implies that truth and existence in mathematics are rooted in shared or individual constructive activity rather than in platonic independent realms; evaluative criteria should therefore be constructive reproducibility and communicability, not metaphysical existence.
